featured.title: ERP Data Mapping Platform
featured.summary: Replaced a spreadsheet-driven ERP import workflow with a purpose-built application. Users had been hand-mapping XLS files into Sage Intacct; the new system let them upload, review, map fields visually, and run large imports asynchronously while continuing to work.
highlights: Visual field mapping replacing manual spreadsheet mapping
Queue-backed import/export so large jobs never block a request
Frontend completion notifications for asynchronous work

featured.title: Shared UI & Design System
featured.summary: A shared component library and CSS foundation distributed over NPM and consumed by both React and Angular applications. Drew architectural cues from Tailwind, Bootstrap, IBM Carbon, and Ramsey's Gazelle — with accessibility built into the primitives rather than documented beside them.
highlights: Framework-agnostic CSS foundation consumed by React and Angular
Design tokens and reusable UI primitives
Accessibility as a property of the components, not a checklist
Contribution path so the system was not a central-team bottleneck

selected.title: Aviation ↔ Sage Intacct Integration
selected.summary: Two systems of record disagreed about the same transactions. The durable fix was not a better sync job — it was deciding, field by field, which system owns what, and making disagreement visible instead of silent.
highlights: Explicit single-owner model for every shared field
Reconciliation automated and surfaced as data

selected.title: LIFE SURGE Platform Systems
selected.summary: Solutions architecture across education, events, registration, payments, and internal platforms — setting system boundaries, integration patterns, API contracts, and AI strategy across multiple engineering teams alongside executive stakeholders.
highlights: System boundaries and ownership models across platforms
Event landing page and registration architecture

selected.title: E-Commerce Modernization
selected.summary: Modernizing legacy jQuery and Handlebars commerce surfaces toward React, across multiple brands and domains — with shared component patterns and the Gazelle design system holding consistency together.
highlights: jQuery/Handlebars → React migration on live commerce surfaces
Reusable frontend architecture across multiple brands

labs.title: Next Level Tutoring
labs.summary: Idea to live business in roughly 96 hours — brand, site, funnel, payments, and marketing launch. Included here for the execution speed, not the engineering depth.

labs.title: Automation & Bots
labs.summary: A run of small event-driven automation projects across Discord, X, and game APIs — OAuth flows, scheduled jobs, and webhook plumbing. Where new integration patterns get tried before they show up in client work.
